exposure: Breastfeeding status (lower rates or cessation of breastfeeding)
outcome: Postpartum depression (PPD) measured by Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)
cohort: The study included 333 Taiwanese pregnant women.
finding: Higher scores on the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) were significantly associated with lower rates or cessation of breastfeeding, identifying it as an important risk factor for Postpartum Depression (PPD).
mod_finding: Caesarean section delivery was identified as a significant risk factor for postpartum depression (Odds ratio: 2.814, CI: 1.617-4.899, p <.001).
